sources.entry: 🧰 Awesome dotfiles: lots of great dotfiles.

summary.one_liner: A curated list of dotfiles resources, including articles, example dotfiles repos, management tools, and related awesome lists.
summary.what_it_does:
The README is a curated Markdown list rather than a tool. It is organized into sections: articles (introductions, tutorials, shell startup, and specific tools like GNU Stow and Ansible), guidance on finding dotfiles repos on GitHub, example dotfiles repositories grouped by shell (Bash, Zsh, Fish) and Ansible with a short focus description for each, and a Tools section listing dotfile managers and related utilities. It also includes miscellaneous references (XDG spec, FHS), related awesome lists, and an archive of abandoned dotfiles projects. Each entry is a link with a one-line description and no code is included.</what_it_does>
<parameter name="how_to_run">[]
use_cases: Finding example dotfiles repos to copy ideas from
Choosing a dotfile manager such as Stow, chezmoi, or yadm
Reading articles on managing dotfiles with Git
Setting up a new Mac development machine
Looking up shell framework options for Zsh, Bash, or Fish
Discovering related awesome lists for shells and dev environments
notable: Covers dotfile managers across many approaches: symlink farms, Git-native, templating, Nix, and Ansible
Example repos are grouped by shell and include focus notes for quick comparison
Includes an archive section of abandoned dotfiles projects, with notes that older tools are often battle-tested
Released under CC0 public domain dedication
caveats: This is a link list, not software; it contains no installable code
Many linked projects and articles may be old or unmaintained, and the archive section lists abandoned ones
The README has no install or run instructions
